You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer driver-run):
- file: driver/shm.hpp:88
- category: stale-doc
- title: allocate() doc promises a printed '[hsim mmap]' line; code logs '[andesim] mmap' at debug level
- detail: shm.hpp:87-91 documents allocate() as: print one '[hsim mmap] <size> at <dir> (free: <free>)' line (plus '; fallback: <why>' when /dev/shm was skipped). The implementation (shm.cpp:209-212) builds '[andesim] mmap <size> at <dir> (free: ...)' with ' (fallback: ...)' - different prefix, different fallback separator - and emits it via log_line(kLogDebug), i.e. only when --log-level >= debug, not unconditionally. tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_log_level.sh:8 explicitly calls '[hsim mmap]' 'the retired prefix', confirming the header comment predates the rename. The header's file-top comment (lines 5-7, 'print one status line that always names the chosen tier') has the same drift.
- claimed safety: Comment-only change; no code or output touched.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.

Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.

BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	// Shared-mmap allocation for andesim.
2	//
3	// The caller asks for `size` bytes; we resolve a backing directory over a
4	// tier list (first fit wins, fit = size + 256 MiB free), allocate a sparse
5	// file with mkstemp+truncate, and print one status line that always names
6	// the chosen tier -- and, when we fell past /dev/shm, why. HSIM_MMAP_DIR
7	// pins a single tier (hard error if it does not fit; no fallback past it).
8	#ifndef ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
9	#define ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
10	
11	#include <functional>
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	namespace andes_sim {
16	
17	// Free-space headroom a tier must have beyond the requested size.
18	inline constexpr long long kMmapSafetyMargin = 256LL * 1024 * 1024;
19	
20	// One backing-store candidate: the directory plus the label used in
21	// status/error messages ("/dev/shm", "~/.cache/andesim", "HSIM_MMAP_DIR=..").
22	struct MmapTier {
23	  std::string dir;
24	  std::string label;
25	};
26	
27	// resolve_mmap_dir result: the chosen dir ("" on failure) and, when a tier
28	// was skipped, a human note saying which and why ("" when tiers[0] fit).
29	struct MmapDirChoice {
30	  std::string dir;
31	  std::string note;
32	};
33	
34	// Parse "8G" / "512M" / "1024" / "1.5G" into a positive byte count. On success
35	// returns the count and leaves `err` empty; on failure returns 0 and sets `err`
36	// to the argparse-style message. Fractional values truncate (1.5G -> whole
37	// bytes).
38	long long parse_size(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);
39	
40	// L26/F2: the physical shared mmap is one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES)
41	// larger than the program's --mem-size, so the V-register transport page sits
42	// just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout -- low stack, top-of-
43	// RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling -- can reach a page past its own
44	// RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. The vsim side parks the scratch
45	// at the mmap's top page (v_scratch_gpa), which equals ram_base + program_bytes.
46	long long physical_mmap_bytes(long long program_bytes);
47	
48	// The largest --mem-size whose physical mmap still fits the 2 GiB AE350 DRAM
49	// window (program_bytes + scratch page <= 2 GiB). --mem-size is capped here.
50	long long max_program_mem_bytes();
51	
52	// First-fit resolver over `tiers`. `probe(dir)` returns the dir's free bytes,
53	// or -1 when it does not exist. A tier fits when probe >= size + margin.
54	// On success `err` is empty; when nothing fits, returns {"", ""} and `err`
55	// names every tier's reason plus the HSIM_MMAP_DIR hint. Pure: no env, no
56	// filesystem -- testable with a fake probe.
57	MmapDirChoice resolve_mmap_dir(
58	    const std::vector<MmapTier>& tiers, long long size,
59	    const std::function<long long(const std::string&)>& probe,
60	    std::string& err);
61	
62	// The andesim cache root: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim, else ~/.cache/andesim,
63	// else "" (no HOME). Shared by the mmap tier list and the repro bundles.
64	std::string andesim_cache_dir();
65	
66	// Build the real tier list from the environment:
67	//   HSIM_MMAP_DIR set -> that single pinned tier;
68	//   else            -> /dev/shm, then $XDG_CACHE_HOME|~/.cache + /andesim
69	//                      (created here so the free-space probe can see it).
70	std::vector<MmapTier> mmap_tiers();
71	
72	// WSL2 advice for `doctor`: given /proc/version contents, the repo dir, and
73	// the mmap tier list, return warning lines. Empty when not on WSL2. On WSL2:
74	// always the .wslconfig memory= hint (tmpfs is capped by the WSL VM), plus a
75	// drvfs warning for the repo or any tier dir under /mnt/ (slow, and
76	// MAP_SHARED is not coherent across the 9p boundary). Pure -- testable.
77	std::vector<std::string> wsl_warnings(const std::string& proc_version,
78	                                      const std::string& repo_dir,
79	                                      const std::vector<MmapTier>& tiers);
80	
81	// Convert a --mem-size spec into the fast leg's plain QEMU `-m` argv:
82	// {"-m", "<MiB>M"}. Empty spec -> {} with no error (QEMU as-is). Malformed
83	// specs and sizes that are not a whole MiB (QEMU's -m granularity) return {}
84	// and set `err`.
85	std::vector<std::string> qemu_m_args(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);
86	
87	// Allocate a sparse mmap file of `size` bytes in the resolved dir (mkstemp +
88	// truncate), print one "[hsim mmap] <size> at <dir> (free: <free>)" line
89	// (plus "; fallback: <why>" when /dev/shm was skipped), and return its path.
90	// On failure returns "" and sets `err`. Caller owns the file (unlink when
91	// done).
92	std::string allocate(long long size, std::string& err,
93	                     const std::string& prefix = "hsim-shm.");
94	
95	}  // namespace andes_sim
96	
97	#endif  // ANDESIM_SHM_HPP
98

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Log-level contract: driver chatter is leveled like vsim's --log-level
3	# (0=trace 1=debug 2=info 3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off; default 2=info).
4	#
5	#   1. default (info): a hybrid --dry-run shows the dry-run commands but NO
6	#      banner and NO mmap line.
7	#   2. --log-level 1 (debug): banner + mmap line appear; the mmap line uses
8	#      the [andesim] prefix and the retired [hsim mmap] prefix is gone.
9	#   3. default (info) on a real hybrid run: program output + the cycle
10	#      figure only -- no banner, no mmap line, no trailing PASS chatter.
11	#   4. an out-of-range --log-level is a clean non-zero error naming 0..6.
12	#
13	# RED-then-green smoke test, run manually during driver development. Not wired
14	# into run_e2e.sh.
15	set -uo pipefail
16	
17	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
18	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
19	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
20	
21	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
22	ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf"
23	ENGINE="vsim:ax45mpv_premium"
24	
25	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
26	[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"
27	[ -f "$ELF" ] || fail "missing fixture: $ELF"
28	
29	# 1. default level hides the banner and the mmap line (dry-run: cheap)
30	out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
31	  || fail "hybrid --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
32	echo "$out" | grep -q "dry-run: 2 command(s)" || fail "dry-run header missing:"$'\n'"$out"
33	echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "default level should hide the banner:"$'\n'"$out"
34	echo "$out" | grep -qi "mmap" && fail "default level should hide the mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"
35	
36	# 2. debug level shows them, with the [andesim] prefix (no [hsim mmap])
37	out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 1 --dry-run "$ELF" 2>&1) \
38	  || fail "hybrid --log-level 1 --dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
39	echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" || fail "debug level missing banner:"$'\n'"$out"
40	echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] mmap" || fail "debug level missing [andesim] mmap line:"$'\n'"$out"
41	echo "$out" | grep -q "\[hsim mmap\]" && fail "[hsim mmap] prefix must be gone:"$'\n'"$out"
42	
43	# 2b. the level is forwarded to both legs (visible in the dry-run commands):
44	#     the QEMU plugin gets log_level=N, the vsim leg gets --log-level N
45	echo "$out" | grep -q "log_level=1" || fail "fast-leg plugin missing log_level=1:"$'\n'"$out"
46	echo "$out" | grep -Eq "sim_[a-z0-9_]+ .*--log-level 1" \
47	  || fail "accurate-leg missing --log-level 1:"$'\n'"$out"
48	
49	# 2c. debug also explains the driver's decisions: engine choice reason ...
50	echo "$out" | grep -q "^\[andesim\] engine: $ENGINE (selected by --engine)$" \
51	  || fail "debug: engine decision line missing:"$'\n'"$out"
52	
53	# ... and pc-trigger symbol resolution
54	out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 1 --dry-run \
55	        --pc-start say_hello --pc-end vplat_roi_end "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf" 2>&1) \
56	  || fail "pc dry-run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
57	echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] trigger pc: say_hello -> 0x[0-9a-fA-F]+, vplat_roi_end -> 0x[0-9a-fA-F]+$' \
58	  || fail "debug: pc resolution line missing:"$'\n'"$out"
59	
60	# 3. default level on a real hybrid run: program output + cycle figure only;
61	#    the answer line uses the same [andesim] N cycles shape as cycle mode,
62	#    with the raw mcycle detail reserved for debug.
63	out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" "$ELF" 2>&1) \
64	  || fail "hybrid run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
65	echo "$out" | grep -q "hello from QEMU1" || fail "program output missing:"$'\n'"$out"
66	echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$' || fail "cycle figure missing:"$'\n'"$out"
67	echo "$out" | grep -q "window_cycles" && fail "old window_cycles format leaked:"$'\n'"$out"
68	echo "$out" | grep -q "mcycle=" && fail "mcycle detail leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
69	echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "banner leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
70	echo "$out" | grep -qi "mmap" && fail "mmap line leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
71	echo "$out" | grep -q "^PASS:" && fail "PASS chatter leaked at default level:"$'\n'"$out"
72	
73	# 3b. debug level adds the window detail line next to the answer, but the
74	#     exec command lines stay trace-only
75	out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 1 "$ELF" 2>&1) \
76	  || fail "hybrid --log-level 1 run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
77	echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$' || fail "debug: cycle figure missing:"$'\n'"$out"
78	echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] window: trigger=marker vsim mcycle=[0-9]+ qemu mcycle=[0-9]+$' \
79	  || fail "debug: window detail line missing:"$'\n'"$out"
80	echo "$out" | grep -q "\[andesim\] exec " && fail "exec lines leaked at debug level:"$'\n'"$out"
81	echo "$out" | grep -q "\[hybrid_handoff\] drained" \
82	  || fail "debug: plugin drain summary not relayed:"$'\n'"$out"
83	
84	# 3c. trace level prints each leg's exact command before spawning it
85	out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --log-level 0 "$ELF" 2>&1) \
86	  || fail "hybrid --log-level 0 run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
87	echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] exec fast-leg \[qemu64\]: .*qemu-system-riscv64' \
88	  || fail "trace: fast-leg exec line missing:"$'\n'"$out"
89	echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] exec accurate-leg \[vsim:ax45mpv_premium\]: .*sim_ax45mpv_premium' \
90	  || fail "trace: accurate-leg exec line missing:"$'\n'"$out"
91	
92	# 3e. trace level prints the standalone command too (fast/cycle share
93	#     run_standalone): without it a wedged fast run is undiagnosable from
94	#     logs -- there is no later step to show the command.
95	out=$("$BIN" --mode fast --log-level 0 "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_exit41.elf" 2>&1)
96	rc=$?
97	[ "$rc" -eq 41 ] || fail "fast vplat_exit41 expected rc 41, got $rc:"$'\n'"$out"
98	echo "$out" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] exec standalone \[qemu64\]: .*qemu-system-riscv64' \
99	  || fail "trace: standalone exec line missing:"$'\n'"$out"
100	
101	# 3d. --log-file captures EVERY level with timestamps while the console
102	#     stays at its threshold (default here: still only output + answer)
103	LOGDIR=$(mktemp -d)
104	trap 'rm -rf "$LOGDIR"' EXIT
105	LOGFILE="$LOGDIR/run.log"
106	out=$("$BIN" --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
107	        --log-file "$LOGFILE" "$ELF" 2>&1) \
108	  || fail "hybrid --log-file run exited non-zero:"$'\n'"$out"
109	echo "$out" | grep -q "model=hybrid" && fail "--log-file must not raise console verbosity:"$'\n'"$out"
110	[ -f "$LOGFILE" ] || fail "log file not created: $LOGFILE"
111	grep -q "model=hybrid" "$LOGFILE" || fail "log file missing debug banner:"$'\n'"$(cat "$LOGFILE")"
112	grep -q "exec fast-leg" "$LOGFILE" || fail "log file missing trace exec line:"$'\n'"$(cat "$LOGFILE")"
113	grep -Eq "\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles" "$LOGFILE" || fail "log file missing answer line:"$'\n'"$(cat "$LOGFILE")"
114	grep -Eq '^\[20[0-9]{2}-[01][0-9]-[0-3][0-9]T' "$LOGFILE" || fail "log file lines missing timestamps:"$'\n'"$(cat "$LOGFILE")"
115	
116	# 4. out-of-range level is a clean error
117	"$BIN" --mode fast --log-level 9 "$ELF" >/dev/null 2>&1 && fail "--log-level 9 should exit non-zero"
118	out=$("$BIN" --mode fast --log-level 9 "$ELF" 2>&1)
119	echo "$out" | grep -q "0=trace" || fail "bad --log-level error should name the scale:"$'\n'"$out"
120
